editorial:
You get a wild ride when a brave woman slips into Kageno Steel Manufacturers to stop a secret plan to take over Japan. The place is packed with strange weapons, creepy bosses, and fighters dressed like geishas, so every hallway feels like a trap. The tone mixes loud action, silly jokes, and sci-fi horror without slowing down, making it feel like a comic book come to life. Even as a short film, it throws you into the chaos fast and keeps the energy high.

The fights are messy in a fun way, with gadgets, blood, and big laughs, though the story is thin and some jokes land harder than others. If you enjoy RoboGeisha-style madness, you will have a blast, but viewers wanting deep characters may feel left out. Watch it for pure late-night entertainment, preferably streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, renting on Apple TV, or grabbing the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest chaos.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the hero reaches the top floor and learns the company leader is a machine built to control Japan. She battles the fearsome geisha corps, triggers the factory to explode, and escapes with proof of the plot. The twist is that her own body has hidden robot parts, hinting she may be the next weapon in line.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves wild Japanese action comedies and late-night cult movies.
